incident-bot: [ALERT] High error rate and timeouts detected: /v1/generate (us-east-1). p95 and p99 latency up >3x after deploy at 12:05UTC (commit abc123). Error type: 504 Gateway Timeout + upstream 5xx. Pager escalated to oncall.

maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it. can someone post the deploy id and which cluster?

deploy-bot: Deploy abc123 -> prod-us-east started at 2026-03-15T12:05:12Z by lucas. Canary cut 5m ago.

ashwin (sre): I'm seeing p95 jump from 220ms -> 1.1s, p99 from 480ms -> 2.8s. 5xx rate went from 0.2% -> 6.8% in last 6m.

maya (oncall): thanks. ashwin, do you have a heatmap or service map? impact on downstream gateways?

ashwin (sre): gateway errors concentrated on inference-proxy group in us-east-1a/b. Multiplex queue length spiked; connection pool saturating. quick graph: (link)

lucas (eng-runtime): i rolled runtime kernel selector change in this canary (abc123). changed default kernel for medium-long contexts to kernel-v2. May be new scheduling path.

riley (sre-lead): this looks like a typical post-deploy latency regression. If rollback is quick, do it. maya, propose immediate rollback of abc123 to previous release abc122 for us-east traffic.

maya (oncall): agree. triggering rollback now.

maya (oncall): /rollback deploy abc123 --to abc122 --region us-east-1

deploy-bot: Received rollback request. Starting rollback of deploy abc123 -> routing traffic back to abc122 across prod-us-east. Estimated 90s to change routing.

noah (customer-support): receiving CS tickets showing 504s on customers in US-EAST. Early triage: ~12 tickets in last 20m, some customers report timeouts in production apps.

ashwin (sre): attaching quick reproducer:
```
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"input":"hello"}' -H 'X-Model: redwood-medium'
HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
content-type: application/json
{"error":"upstream timeout after 30000ms","attempts":3}
```

lucas (eng-runtime): logs from runtime nodes:
```
[2026-03-15T12:13:02Z] WARN kernel-selector: selected kernel-v2 for model:redwood-medium seq_len_est:1024
[2026-03-15T12:13:02Z] ERROR dispatch: request stuck in multiplex queue > 20s (queue_len=128)
[2026-03-15T12:13:03Z] WARN kvcache: eviction spike, mem_pressure true
```

ashwin (sre): hypothesis: new kernel path causing slower per-token scheduling with high concurrency -> queueing -> connection pool exhaustion -> upstream 504s. Also kvcache eviction causing extra latency on long contexts.

tess (product-ops): any customer-visible SLA hits? estimate minutes of impact and percent of requests?

ashwin (sre): rough estimate: peak 6.8% errors for ~18 minutes in us-east. Global traffic routed across regions so overall impact ~1.1% of global requests.

noah (customer-support): posting to status page: "We are investigating increased timeouts for text generation in US-East. Some requests may return 504s; work underway to rollback recent deploy." will update every 15m.

deploy-bot: Rollback progress: routing change applied to 60% of producers (90s elapsed).

maya (oncall): monitoring metrics now — ashwin, riley, lucas watch telemetry for p95/p99 and 5xx.

ashwin (sre): p99 started to come down after routing change at t+3m. once 100% rolled back, p99 at baseline 520ms, 5xx rate ~0.25%.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. All us-east traffic back to abc122.

riley (sre-lead): good. confirm mitigation: rollback effective and service healthy. Initiating incident severity reduction.

tess (product-ops): will notify execs with summary. noah, patch status page and CS updates?

noah (customer-support): status updated: "Degraded -> Mitigated". followup will include timeline & root cause once we have postmortem.

lucas (eng-runtime): collecting runtime traces and kernel perf profiles from canary nodes. I'll upload to the incident ticket. preliminary note: kvcache eviction and a change in the poller wake strategy hit worst under multiplex concurrency.

ashwin (sre): created incident ticket INC-2026-0315-01 and assigned to eng-runtime + SRE for RCA. I'll add load-shed rule to limit concurrent multiplex in config as a temporary safety.

maya (oncall): handing off to riley / eng-runtime for detailed investigation. I'm clear to go back to rotation at 12:45UTC.

riley (sre-lead): taking ownership for post-incident. next steps: collect perf traces, reproduce in staging with kernel-v2 under load, confirm fix (revert kernel change or add safety throttle), publish postmortem by EOD+1.

tess (product-ops): escalate notes: customers impacted small but visible; recommend proactively offering support to top 5 customers who filed tickets.

noah (customer-support): will triage and send proactive messages to affected customers.

lucas (eng-runtime): quick mitigation idea: add kvcache prefetch/backoff and reduce multiplex concurrency threshold for kernel-v2 to avoid queue blowup. will prototype in canary before re-landing kernel change.

riley (sre-lead): agreed. Do not re-deploy kernel-v2 to production until we've validated under load.

maya (oncall): closing pager. marking incident as mitigated. keep thread open for RCA updates. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status: MITIGATED. Incident ticket INC-2026-0315-01 created. Postmortem owner: riley.

riley (sre-lead): will post initial timeline and action items in INC-2026-0315-01 by EOD. thanks all for fast rollback and coordination.

noah (customer-support): final note: 12 CS tickets, 3 high-priority customers contacted; CS followups scheduled."
